title: Nokia Ruled Smartphones. Then Apple Ended It
source: Nokia smartphone (Symbian, then early Lumia) unit shipments and Apple iPhone fiscal-year unit sales, compiled from IDC/Gartner/Strategy Analytics quarterly trackers and company reports. Nokia shipped a then-record ~100 million smartphones in 2010 (IDC); its global smartphone share halved from 33% in 2010 to 16% in 2011 as Apple became the world's largest smartphone vendor by volume in Q4 2011 (Strategy Analytics: Apple 37M vs Nokia 19.6M that quarter). Nokia's full-year total collapsed to roughly 30-35 million by 2012-2013 as Symbian was wound down and Lumia never scaled; Apple's iPhone unit sales are from Apple's 10-K filings (FY2008-FY2013). Figures approximate and rounded to the nearest million.
